# bambu-mcp

bambu-mcp is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that lets AI
agents monitor and control Bambu Lab printers. It is built on bambu-printer-manager and keeps
one live MQTT session per configured printer. The same process also serves a REST API and
MJPEG camera streams.

Source: [synman/bambu-mcp](https://github.com/synman/bambu-mcp) on GitHub.

## At a glance

| Surface | Count | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| MCP tools | 101 (49 read-only, 52 write, 50 need `user_permission=True`) | [MCP Tools](tools/index.md) |
| REST API routes | 81 | [REST API](rest-api.md) |
| MCP resources | 4 rules files plus 1 alert feed template | [Resources](#resources-and-prompt) |
| MCP prompts | 1 (`bambu_system_context`) | [Resources](#resources-and-prompt) |

## Requirements

- Python 3.12 or newer.
- Each printer powered on and on the same local network as the server.
- Each printer's IP address, serial number and access code. The access code is on the
  printer's touchscreen under Settings, Network.

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/synman/bambu-mcp.git
cd bambu-mcp
python3 make.py
```

Run `make.py` with Python 3.12 or newer, for example `python3.12 make.py`: the virtual
environment uses the interpreter that runs it. `make.py` creates a `.venv` inside the project and installs bambu-mcp with its dependencies,
including bambu-printer-manager from its `devel` branch. Run it again to pick up dependency
updates.

## Running the server

| Transport | Command | Listens on |
|---|---|---|
| stdio (default) | `.venv/bin/python3 server.py` | the client's stdin and stdout |
| Streamable HTTP | `.venv/bin/python3 server.py --transport streamable-http` | `http://127.0.0.1:25099/mcp` |
| SSE | `.venv/bin/python3 server.py --transport sse` | `http://127.0.0.1:8000/sse` |

In Streamable HTTP mode only one server runs per machine. If port 25099 is taken it scans
down to 25000 and writes the port it chose to `~/.bambu-mcp/daemon.port`. Every transport connects to the configured printers in the background, so
tools answer at once and printer data arrives as each session connects. When at least one
printer is configured at startup, the server also starts the REST API.

## Client configuration

A stdio client starts the server itself and talks to it over stdin and stdout. Point it at
the project's Python and `server.py`. The repo ships
`config/claude_desktop.example.json` for Claude Desktop:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bambu-mcp": {
      "command": "<install-dir>/bambu-mcp/.venv/bin/python3",
      "args": ["<install-dir>/bambu-mcp/server.py"],
      "env": {
        "PYTHONPATH": "<install-dir>/bambu-mcp"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`config/copilot_mcp.example.json` is the same entry for GitHub Copilot CLI. A client that
speaks Streamable HTTP can connect to a running server at `http://127.0.0.1:25099/mcp`
instead, using the port in `~/.bambu-mcp/daemon.port` if it differs.

## Adding a printer

1. Call `discover_printers` to find printers on the local network by SSDP.
2. Read the access code from the printer's touchscreen.
3. Call `add_printer` with the name, IP address, serial number and access code, and
   `user_permission=True`.
4. Call `get_printer_state` with the new name to confirm the session is live.

Printer credentials are stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM. The master key comes from the
`BAMBU_MCP_SECRETS_KEY` environment variable, else the OS keychain, else a local key file.

## Safety model

- **Write guard.** Every tool that changes printer or server state refuses unless called
  with `user_permission=True`. Without it the tool changes nothing and returns a refusal
  that names the consequence. The [MCP Tools](tools/index.md) page marks each one.
- **Active-print guard.** Tools that would disturb a running print refuse while the printer
  is printing or preparing, even with `user_permission=True`.
- **Tool annotations.** Every tool declares a title and read-only, destructive, idempotent
  and open-world hints, so a client can grant read-only tools on their own.

## REST API

The REST API exposes the same printer sessions over HTTP. Its port comes from a shared pool
starting at 49152, so it is not fixed. Find it with the `get_server_info` tool or
`GET /api/server_info`. The running server also publishes a Swagger UI at `/api/docs` and the
OpenAPI document at `/api/openapi.json`.

!!! warning "No authentication"
    The REST API and the camera streams listen on all network interfaces and ask for no
    credentials. Anyone who can reach the port can read printer state, and the REST API
    accepts commands. Run bambu-mcp only on a trusted network.

Full route list: [REST API](rest-api.md).

## Camera streams

`start_stream` and `view_stream` start a local MJPEG server for a printer's camera, on a
port from the same pool. The camera protocol follows the printer model:

| Protocol | Models |
|---|---|
| RTSPS, port 322 | X1C, X1, X1E, P2S, H2D, H2S |
| TLS, port 6000 | A1, A1 Mini, P1P, P1S |

`get_snapshot` returns a URL for one still frame without starting a stream.

## Resources and prompt

| URI or name | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `bambu://rules/global` | The server host's global agent rules file, with IPs, serials and credentials redacted |
| `bambu://rules/printer-app` | The bambu-printer-app agent rules file, redacted |
| `bambu://rules/printer-manager` | The bambu-printer-manager agent rules file, redacted |
| `bambu://rules/bambu-mcp` | The bambu-mcp agent rules file, redacted |
| `bambu://alerts/{name}` | Pending state-change alerts for one printer as JSON, without clearing them |
| `bambu_system_context` (prompt) | Safety rules and tool guidance to load at the start of a session |

The rules resources read files from the server's home directory, so their content depends on
the machine running the server.
